summary: The candidate survives every dispatched semantic attack. It mints no numeric quality threshold; keeps the five areas explicitly illustrative and manifest-bounded; carries all four DR-006 recipe dependencies without settling them; retains TypeScript as the sole slice-1 role; keeps DR-118 ineligible for D-056 Class B; makes no SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, or implementation claim; answers every acceptance-cell obligation; and reproduces file 02 lines 308-338 plus the unique live DR-118 row exactly. Acceptance is withheld for one evidence-provenance defect: recordedInputs names the live COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md path but pins historical 12d192f7... bytes, while the live path measures d210f103..., without labeling the pin historical or recording a live remeasurement. The three cited decision sections are byte-identical across those versions, so this is not a semantic blocker. Two advisories preserve D-007's runner/environment observation and the still-open DR-125 boundary dependency. At 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, DR-118 remains DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED and this verdict authorizes no implementation.

advisories.title: Performance-baseline rows should explicitly record runner and environment
advisories.detail: The digest-pinned D-007 consent records OBS-D007-T2-01: a performance baseline measures nothing reproducibly unless its runner/environment is recorded, and routes explicit environment recording to matrix authoring and the DR-G13/G14 checklist. The candidate requires a measurement method, which can reasonably include environment and is why this is nonblocking, but it does not name runner/environment explicitly. Add it to the per-row performance-baseline fields when the matrix is authored.

advisories.title: The DR-125 capability-boundary dependency should be stated as an open activation gate
advisories.detail: The live DR-125 row is OPEN. D-007 OBS-D007-T2-02 says the coherent boundary is manifest-instantiates-host-contract and that DR-103 and DR-125 must close before matrix authoring. This candidate does not claim DR-125 accepted and does not author a matrix, so it does not treat an unaccepted sibling as settled. Explicitly recording the closure dependency and divergence owner would keep later matrix authoring from mistaking the referenced contract for an already-live capability vocabulary.
